base.name: AP-1 · Base of Operations
base.description: Primary base on the Sinuous Unit. Considered the safest site in the study: slopes below 5° at 10 m scale and almost no rocks larger than 1 m. About 10 cm of sand over up to 80 m of ice.

pois.name: AP-9 · ISRU Site
pois.description: Primary heavy-ISRU site on the Sinuous Unit. Thickest subsurface ice of the unit (radar: up to ~80 m of excess ice) and the unit's highest combined ice-consistency index. Rougher and rockier than AP-1.

pois.name: APMR · Paleo-megaripples
pois.description: Paleo-megaripples and lithified dunes east of AP-9, at the far end of Route 1 across the Sinuous Unit.

pois.name: HCP · Polygon Field
pois.description: Field of high-centered thermal-contraction polygons (HiRISE ESP_037655_2210). A modal polygon diameter of ~11 m suggests ground ice only ~6–20 cm deep; this depth is a model-based estimate calibrated at the Phoenix site, not a direct measurement.

pois.name: AP-8 · Periglacial Plain
pois.description: Periglacial plain next to the Sinuous Unit. Highest neutron and combined ice indices among adjacent sites, and a basal radar reflector deeper than ~20 m. Shallow ice mining and astrobiology target.

pois.name: US1 · Ogive Front
pois.description: Terminal lobe of Sinuous Unit 1, with ogives and crescent-shaped ridges. Low-insolation NNW–NE scarps preserved for over 20 Myr are candidates for trenching or horizontal drilling. Glaciology target.
